automation_evidence.finding: Industrial robots raised labor productivity and value added across a panel of industries in 17 countries, 1993-2007; the authors estimate robot use raised countries' average annual growth rates by about 0.37 percentage points, with no significant effect on total hours worked. This is the closest well-identified evidence that automation in this sector raises output per worker rather than only cutting headcount.

US commuting-zone study, 1990-2007: one additional robot per thousand workers reduced the employment-to-population ratio by roughly 0.18-0.34 percentage points and lowered wages. Relevant warning that labour-saving automation in fabrication can suppress local hiring even as output holds.

Staggered rollout of a generative-AI conversational assistant to 5,179 customer-support agents raised issues resolved per hour by 14% on average, with a 34% gain for novice/low-skilled agents and minimal effect on experienced staff; customer sentiment and retention also improved. Best available causal estimate for agent-style tools on coordination-heavy desk work, though the setting is support, not manufacturing.

Near-universe of US online vacancies, 2010-2018: AI-exposed establishments were reducing hiring in non-AI positions, but no discernible relationship between AI exposure and employment or wage growth appeared at occupation or industry level - i.e. task-level substitution without detectable aggregate effects yet.

Benchmark study on the public AI4I 2020 milling-machine dataset: gradient-boosted trees and random forests performed best for fault prediction, with process temperature, torque and rotational speed the dominant predictors. Demonstrates feasibility of predictive-maintenance modelling on standard sensor data, but reports model accuracy on a benchmark dataset, not measured downtime or cost savings in a plant.

Preprint on federated learning plus transfer learning for industrial visual inspection of label defects: 95.5% (homogeneous) and 94.2% (heterogeneous) word-level recognition accuracy, with models trained without sharing local plant data. Supports the private/on-prem architecture argument for inspection AI, but is a single-dataset preprint with no production economics.

Field tests of AI-assisted autonomous mobile robots and AGVs for asset inspection and truck loading across three real use cases (rail, port, logistics); one-stage object-detection models performed well enough to be judged actionable outside the lab. Peer-reviewed and field-based, but reports detection performance only - no time saved, error-rate or labour-hour metrics.

US manufacturing-sector labor productivity rose 0.3% in Q3 2026 (durables +2.2%, nondurables -1.7%) and 0.4% year over year, while manufacturing unit labor costs rose 2.7% as hourly compensation rose 3.0%. Government benchmark showing the thin productivity cushion against which automation ROI is being sold.

common_tools: ERP / shop-floor systems: SAP S/4HANA, Oracle NetSuite, Epicor Kinetic, Infor CloudSuite Industrial, Microsoft Dynamics 365 Supply Chain; job-shop MRP such as JobBOSS2 and E2 Shoptech
MES / SCADA / historians: Rockwell FactoryTalk, AVEVA System Platform, Inductive Automation Ignition, Siemens Opcenter
CNC/CAM and machine-tool software: Mastercam, Fusion 360, Siemens NX; machine controllers from Haas, Fanuc, Mazak
CMMS / maintenance: Fiix, UpKeep, eMaint, MaintainX
Quality management (QMS) and SPC: MasterControl, ETQ Reliance, InfinityQS
Labeling and traceability: Loftware, BarTender, NiceLabel; food traceability platforms such as TraceGains and FoodLogiQ
WMS / barcode / handheld scanning layered on the ERP, often with separate shipping and EDI systems for retailer compliance
Actual day-to-day record keeping in many small and mid-size shops: shared spreadsheets, emailed work orders, paper travelers and whiteboards
constraints: Food and beverage producers face FDA FSMA section 204 traceability: lot-level Critical Tracking Events and Key Data Elements must be kept and produced to FDA within 24 hours, including an electronic sortable spreadsheet - so agents touching lot data must write into validated, auditable systems (source: https://www.fda.gov/food/food-safety-modernization-act-fsma/fsma-final-rule-requirements-additional-traceability-records-certain-foods)

Machine safety rules (OSHA 1910.212 machine guarding, 1910.147 lockout/tagout) mean no agent output may directly actuate or bypass guarded equipment; agents advise humans who perform the physical action (general regulatory knowledge; OSHA pages could not be opened in this session and are not cited)

Export-controlled and defense/aerospace work (ITAR/EAR) makes customer drawings, process parameters and bill-of-material data unsuitable for public cloud models; inference is that private or on-prem deployment is preferred for these shops

Customer-owned IP and tooling drawings, plus supplier pricing, are commercially sensitive; most shops will resist sending them to third-party APIs without contractual controls (inference from the nature of contract manufacturing, not from a cited source)

Food safety and quality audits (HACCP/FDA preventive controls, SQF/BRCGS schemes) require documented, version-controlled records and traceable approvals, so agent-generated records need an audit trail
New Jersey environmental and right-to-know reporting (NJ DEP permits, community right-to-know chemical inventories) creates periodic reporting work that is document-heavy and error-sensitive

Legacy reality: many plants run older PLCs and ERPs with no API, so integration is often file-drop, screen-scraping or barcode middleware rather than clean connectors (practitioner observation, not a cited finding)
trends: New Jersey manufacturing employment is roughly flat to slightly declining: about 249,900 jobs (preliminary) with a -0.6% 12-month change, after moving between roughly 247,800 and 249,900 across recent months (BLS NJ Economy at a Glance, 2026)

Margin pressure: manufacturing unit labor costs +2.7% in Q3 2026 against productivity growth of only 0.3%, i.e. compensation is outrunning output per hour (BLS Productivity and Costs, Q3 2026 preliminary)
Nondurable manufacturing (much of NJ food, chemical and consumer packaging) is the weaker half: productivity fell 1.7% in Q3 2026 while durables rose 2.2% (BLS, Q3 2026)
Hiring friction persists nationally: 7.5 million job openings and 3.4 million quits in September 2026 (BLS JOLTS), consistent with continued difficulty filling skilled trades and machine operators

Skilled-trades wage premiums are visible in the data: NJ industrial machinery mechanics ($74,760 median) and first-line production supervisors ($81,110) earn far more than operators ($37,620-$40,280), which is where maintenance and supervisory coordination work concentrates

Automation is already embedded in the sector's economics - robot exposure has measurably shifted employment and wages in exposed local labour markets - so agent projects are usually competing with, or feeding, an existing capital-automation program rather than starting from zero

Seasonal and promotional demand swings (food production, seasonal packaging runs, year-end shipping) concentrate overtime and temporary staffing in specific windows; inference is that scheduling and expediting roles absorb most of that volatility, which is where coordination agents have the clearest recurring pain
caveats: Evidence quality is uneven and mostly indirect for this specific ask. (1) No New Jersey or Middlesex County study measuring time saved, error reduction or revenue recovered from AI agents in light industrial shops was found; every quantified automation result cited here is either macro/industry-level (robots, cross-country or commuting-zone panels), a different task domain (customer support), or a benchmark/preprint result. (2) The strongest causal papers (Graetz & Michaels; Acemoglu & Restrepo) are about industrial robots over 1990-2007, not software agents, and the displacement findings are a caution rather than a sales case. (3) Wage figures come from BLS OEWS May 2025 data as republished by O*NET's state wage pages; they are statewide New Jersey medians, with the New York-Newark-Jersey City metro used as the nearest metro proxy - the Edison-New Brunswick metropolitan division was not separately retrievable, so Middlesex County-specific medians are not shown. (4) The team assembler figure is reported by BLS from the broader 'Miscellaneous Assemblers and Fabricators' group, which may differ from a strict team-assembler definition. (5) The arXiv and PMC items report model accuracy on benchmark or single-dataset problems; they show technical feasibility, not plant-level economics, and are rated Low accordingly. (6) The common_tools list is analyst/practitioner observation of the software landscape, not a sourced market survey - no vendor market-share data was verified. (7) Constraints other than the FDA traceability rule are stated from general regulatory knowledge because OSHA and some state pages could not be opened; they are flagged inline rather than given citations. (8) Search tooling was rate-limited during this session, so discovery relied on direct retrieval of government, O*NET, NBER and arXiv sources; coverage of trade publications, Census AI-adoption microdata and vendor case studies is therefore absent, and the absence of such sources should not be read as absence of evidence.
